name: Nov 1 2026 dev run 107: repeat-check stage (G01-DUP-1, G01-DUP-2)
note: Real rows from the Oct 31 production copy, trimmed to the 2 OUR Center printed stories and the 10 newest others. Answers recorded from deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 at effort low on Nov 1 2026. The recorded same-story prompt held all 265 printed rows; both answers were null, so the trim does not change them.

candidates.headline: OUR Center tightens residency proof to 60 days for St. Vrain Valley assistance
candidates.why: The center's published access rules state the residency requirement for financial assistance was cut from 90 days to 60 days as of Aug. 4, 2025 — a change in who qualifies for help.

candidates.headline: Parkway Food Hall sets Nov. 21 Fall Festival and Chili Cook-Off with $20 tickets
candidates.why: A specific new dated event was posted to the food hall's calendar: a Nov. 21 fall festival and chili cook-off with ticketed admission.

existing.headline: Inn Between of Longmont plans Nov. 5 chili cook-off fundraiser at Bootstrap Brewery
existing.why: The homeless-services nonprofit is promoting a chili contest at Bootstrap Brewery where residents can enter a recipe or come judge, alongside its note about a 25% tax credit for donations.

printed.headline: RTD says its $156 million share of the Fort Collins rail line is unapproved
printed.dek: It separates the $5.58 million for design work approved in April from the $156 million estimate it has not approved, as voters decide Ballot Issue 7A on Nov. 3.
printed.lead_headline: RTD clarifies what its board has and has not approved for Front Range rail Joint Service
printed.lead_why: RTD published a statement distinguishing board-approved funding from unapproved items for intercity passenger rail Joint Service on the Northwest Corridor, tied to the Front Range Passenger Rail project.

printed.headline: CDOT warns the Nov. 1 clock change puts migrating wildlife in rush hour traffic
printed.dek: Troopers investigated 3,811 crashes involving wildlife last year, and a new optional $5 vehicle registration fee takes effect Jan. 1 to pay for crossings.
printed.lead_headline: CDOT warns Nov. 1 clock change puts wildlife on Northern Colorado roads at dusk
printed.lead_why: CDOT and Colorado Parks and Wildlife said the end of daylight saving time on Sunday, Nov. 1 shifts dusk earlier and into rush hour as wildlife migrates.

printed.headline: Boulder County guides offer free health plan help as open enrollment starts Nov. 1
printed.dek: Six in-person appointment days in Longmont are part of the county's free help comparing and enrolling in 2027 plans before a Jan. 15 deadline.
printed.lead_headline: Boulder County Health Coverage Guides available as Connect for Health Colorado enrollment opens Nov. 1
printed.lead_why: Boulder County announced free help comparing and enrolling in health plans as the state exchange's open enrollment begins Nov. 1.

printed.headline: Colorado Gives Day early giving opens Nov. 1, and Aftersight's page is live
printed.dek: Donors can give to Aftersight and more than 5,000 other Colorado nonprofits now, nearly six weeks before the Dec. 8 giving day.
printed.lead_headline: Colorado Gives Day early giving opens Sunday, Nov. 1; Aftersight says donors can give now
printed.lead_why: Aftersight announced that Colorado Gives Day early giving begins Nov. 1 and that its own giving page is already live, a dated statewide fundraising event starting in the next 24 hours.

printed.headline: Shock Art artists wrap up 10 new boxes in Longmont
printed.dek: Ten artists finish painting utility boxes as the Oct. 31 deadline arrives.
printed.lead_headline: New Shock Art artists finish repainting Longmont's electric boxes
printed.lead_why: The Times-Call reported Friday that new and returning Shock Art artists put finishing touches on Longmont's utility boxes.

printed.headline: Today in town — Saturday, Oct. 31
printed.dek: 34 events on Longmont's public calendars today.

printed.headline: Boulder County offices close Nov. 3; elections office and vote centers stay open
printed.dek: Longmont voters can use six vote centers and five 24-hour drop boxes that day for ballots on Questions 3C and 3D, which are due at 7 p.m.
printed.lead_headline: Boulder County government offices close Nov. 3, but the Elections Division stays open for ballot return
printed.lead_why: Boulder County announced that its offices — except the Elections Division — will be closed Tuesday, Nov. 3, which is the same day Longmont ballots for Questions 3C and 3D are due back.

printed.headline: Firehouse Art Center's Dia de Muertos exhibition closes Sunday after two extra days
printed.dek: "Remembering is Resistance," which pairs artists with immigrant storytellers, runs through Nov. 1 at the free downtown Longmont gallery, two days beyond the closing date the city published.
printed.lead_headline: Firehouse Art Center's Día de Muertos exhibition 'Remembering is Resistance' closes Nov. 1
printed.lead_why: The gallery posted a stated closing date for a themed exhibition that opened Oct. 9.

printed.headline: Black advocacy group asks Weiser to review Longmont police killing of Dariss Yearby
printed.dek: The Epitome of Black Excellence and Partnership cited a Taser offer missing from the district attorney's decision letter, and Longmont says its attorney is reading the request.
printed.lead_headline: Black advocacy group asks Colorado attorney general to review Longmont police killing of Dariss Yearby
printed.lead_why: A day after the Boulder County DA declined to charge Officer Joshua Barry, an advocacy group publicly asked the state attorney general to review the fatal shooting — a new development in a story we filed Oct. 29.

printed.headline: Longmont to show proposed Sandstone Ranch Phase 4 ballfields at Nov. 10 meeting
printed.dek: A contractor is already signed to build the four fields, and city staff say the preliminary design is still being adjusted around a creek setback and a sewer line.
printed.lead_headline: Longmont to host Nov. 10 open house on Sandstone Ranch Phase 4 ballfields
printed.lead_why: The city announced a 90-minute Nov. 10 public open house to present plans for the final Sandstone Ranch phase, a four-field ballfield complex.

printed.headline: OUR Center pages list different Community Market visit frequencies
printed.dek: Undated service pages say financial-assistance participants need 60 days’ residency in the St. Vrain Valley School District, with Erie excluded and Allenspark included.
printed.lead_headline: OUR Center publishes service access requirements, including 60-day St. Vrain residency rule
printed.lead_why: A concrete eligibility rule for a Longmont safety-net provider, useful to residents seeking financial assistance and community market access.

printed.headline: OUR Center Marks 40 Years in Longmont With Sept. 26 Celebration at 220 Collyer St.
printed.dek: The nonprofit that grew out of 26 churches and a wave of 1986 closures now serves thousands of St. Vrain Valley households a year — and says demand still outruns its resources.
printed.lead_why: Filed from the Write a story box.
